controls.label: LORRI
controls.description: Taken 6,628 km from Arrokoth. Bright patches and the neck are visible in the original grayscale exposure. The photographed lighting is retained; unseen and grazing surfaces remain gridded.
controls.title: New Horizons close approach

controls.label: False color
controls.description: Near-infrared, red and blue bands reveal color differences across the two lobes. The mission team aligned the bands and matched their blur. This is false color, not a human-visible reconstruction, at 340 metres per native pixel; the grid marks unsupported coverage.
controls.summary: Near-infrared, red and blue bands show spectral differences at 340 metres per native pixel. This is false color; the grid marks unsupported coverage.
controls.title: New Horizons false color

controls.label: Modeled albedo
controls.description: Fitted from 30 New Horizons approach observations on 31 December 2018 and 1 January 2019. Grayscale shows the released albedo values. Uniform areas are unconstrained model fill; the archive supplies no coverage mask. This is a fitted surface model, not a global photograph.
controls.title: New Horizons LORRI albedo model

controls.label: Shape model
controls.description: Released New Horizons contact-binary shape: two overlapping closed lobe meshes. Southern surface detail is constrained by flyby imagery; the unseen side is a source model estimate. Revised pole from the bundled Porter paper Table 2. Its PDS XML gives an inconsistent earlier pole; the paper pole is used with arbitrary meridian and no precision spin-phase claim. The grid marks unmapped terrain.
controls.title: Published New Horizons shape
